ce_bugs.text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync endpoint returns a fetch Response but this caller reads the provider client's res.data shape, so parent-supplied tokens are never parsed and Google refreshes fail.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The new helper returns a Zod SafeParse result rather than credential data, and this stores { success, data } as the Google credential so later consumers cannot read access_token or expiry_date.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod SafeParse wrapper (`{success,data}`), and it is persisted as-is via `data: { key }`, so the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails for every refreshed Google credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal "[object Object]", so `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is effectively `{access_token: string}` with all other keys (expiry, refresh_token, instance_url, etc.) stripped in credential-sync mode; the intended "any numeric property is expiry" rule never applies.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60 — If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the header is absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the secret check passes; the handler relies entirely on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (defined outside this diff) to gate that case.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:97 — findFirst` on `{userId, appId}` picks an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app (e.g. multiple Google accounts) and overwrites it; the update also never resets `invalid: false`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after fresh keys are synced.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys evaluate to literal property names rather than wildcards, so the shared sync schema silently stops enforcing its stated expiry-field contract and future integrations will rely on a misleading boundary.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — This shared parser takes `any` and `ZodTypeAny`, so replacing provider schemas with the sync schema erases the credential shape at the OAuth boundary and lets incompatible persisted keys compile.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every SalesforceCalendarService construction refreshes and persists the token, adding a remote call and database write to each Salesforce calendar operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync path returns a raw Fetch Response although Google and HubSpot read provider token fields directly, so expired shared credentials fail to refresh and retry on each use.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The new parent credential-sync request has no timeout, so a stalled parent application can hold calendar and video refresh requests until runtime timeout.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Shared-secret comparison uses `!==` rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual, making it timing-sensitive.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret header/signature) and the parent app returns live access tokens for any calcomUserId, so the sync endpoint must be unauthenticated or rely on network trust; the response is also trusted unvalidated.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted payload is JSON.parse'd and written verbatim to credential.key with no per-app schema validation; symmetricDecrypt is called with "" when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, and both failures surface as unhandled 500s.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The credential-sync validation branch has no test with a normal token payload, so the computed "[object Object]" required key can reject every refresh response and break token renewal.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — No refresh-path test asserts the Prisma credential payload, leaving the new SafeParse wrapper stored as `key` undetected and making the persisted Google credential unusable on its next read.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — The new webhook has no authentication test for an unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so requests with no header are accepted and can create or replace credentials.

mrv_findings.text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — [P1, confidence 100] `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` now persists the `{ success: true, data: ... }` safeParse envelope through `data: { key }` instead of credential fields, so even a normal non-sync refresh makes the next service construction fail `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `return response;` returns an unread Fetch Response in sync mode while its callbacks return provider-specific objects, so Google's `const token = res?.data;` produces undefined and HubSpot's `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`/`expiresIn` are absent, breaking refresh despite a successful sync endpoint response.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — [P1, confidence 100] `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),` create literal object keys rather than wildcard field schemas, so Zod strips actual expiry and provider fields from sync responses and Office365 persists its old expired `expires_in`, repeatedly refreshing instead of honoring the returned expiry.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) {` chooses the reduced schema globally although `refreshOAuthTokens` bypasses sharing for credentials without a userId, so team Office365 credentials refreshed directly with Microsoft lose the real returned refresh token and are overwritten by `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";`, making their next direct refresh fail.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — [P2, confidence 100] `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` now forces a token-endpoint request for every client construction even with a valid access token, making all Salesforce operations fail during token-endpoint outages while the resulting connection still uses the old `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token,` and may refresh a second time.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — [P2, confidence 100] `const reqBody = appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` has no validation-error handling (nor do the decrypt/JSON parse operations below), so an authenticated caller submitting a missing field, malformed ciphertext, or invalid decrypted JSON receives an unhandled 500 instead of a non-retryable client-error response.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.update({` references an identifier with no import or declaration in this module, so type-checking fails and a successful Salesforce refresh throws ReferenceError before constructing the client.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:3 — [P1, confidence 75] `import type { IntegrationOAuthCallbackState } from "../../types";` (also in encodeOAuthState.ts:3) resolves to app-store/_utils/types after the extra oauth directory was introduced instead of app-store/types, leaving both OAuth helpers with an unresolved type dependency.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.create({` runs for any accepted team member and returns before `await throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId });`, allowing a non-admin to install team credentials, including their own Stripe payment account, through a crafted OAuth teamId.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — [P1, confidence 75] `body: new URLSearchParams({` sends only `calcomUserId: userId.toString(),` and `appSlug,` with no authentication or signature, so a sync endpoint reachable by other callers that accepts this request cannot distinguish Cal.com from an attacker requesting another user's access token.
